contenders.handicapper_notes: Granted Post-Scratch Lone Speed (+6) boost as the undisputed early speed runner in this depleted field. Comes off back-to-back runner-up finishes over 1100m, including a gritty second at this track and trip on October 18 when leading until the shadows of the post. Inherits the fence (barrier 1) following scratchings and gets the booking of top jockey Brodie Loy (21% strike rate). With an uncontested lead on Good 3 ground, he is poised to break his maiden.

The primary threat and logical danger horse. Strips much fitter second-up for the powerful Matthew Dale and Nick Heywood combination after a solid fourth over 1200m at Goulburn where he sat handy and ground to the line. Dropping back to 1100m suits his sharp Capitalist pedigree. Will camp in the box-seat stalking the lone leader (P style) and gets the uphill 405m home straight to mount his challenge.

Hard-fit 4yo mare from the Natalie Jarvis yard who brings proven country maiden figures, placing in four of 15 starts. Fought on well for third at Albury last start after receiving interference early. Carries 57.0kg and possesses a reliable swooping kick (S style) that will benefit from the spacious Nowra outer circuit, though her 0-for-15 career record highlights an inability to put races away.

Eight-year-old mare who is still a maiden after 34 career outings. Put in an improved run when fourth beaten 2 lengths over 1400m at this course in September, but she drops back sharply to 1100m off a six-week freshening. Lack of early tactical pace will see her settle well back as a closer (C) and she is playing for minor prize money only.

Resumes from a lengthy 132-day spell without any recorded official barrier trials. Was well beaten when eighth at Goulburn in June after being reported lame post-race. Winless in 15 attempts and unplaced in four starts on dry ground. Entitled to need this outing before finding true race fitness.

Canonical style S will relish the 405m uphill Nowra home straight.

Warwick Farm shipper for Gary Portelli who produced an excellent third in Canberra Class 1 company over 2000m on October 23, beaten just 0.7 lengths after suffering early contact and racing wide. Warwick Farm-trained mare who bounced back to form when third in BM65 grade at Canberra over 2000m on October 9. Proven staying winner over 2100m at Wyong earlier this year. Well treated under set-weight conditions at 57kg. Canonical style P should track into the race before the home turn.

Hawkesbury visitor stepping out on a quick seven-day turnaround after placing third in a BM50 at Mudgee over 2000m. Previously runner-up in BM58 company over 2000m at Moruya. Possesses forward tactical intent to settle close to the speed, though still a maiden after 20 attempts.

Made solid late ground when sixth beaten under three lengths behind Pure Melody and Babyfaced Assassin at Canberra over 2000m on October 23. Stretches out to 2200m for the first time. Canonical style S will drop out and look to make one sustained charge up the rise.

Finished sixth beaten nearly six lengths at Kembla Grange over 2000m in Class 1 company five weeks ago. Drawn softly in barrier 1 to save ground, but remains unplaced in ten career starts and stamina past 2000m is completely unproven.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Maps ideally from the inside draw under canonical 'P' style to trail contested speed between Girls Weekend and Jazz All Knight. Brings strong provincial formlines (3rd in Kembla BM64 two back) and excels around Archer Racecourse with an unblemished top-three track record (3: 1-1-1). Forgive her last-start excuse at Newcastle where she suffered severe crowding. Gets weight relief down to 57.5kg and will relish the 405m uphill charge.

Brings the highest recent speed ratings into the event, having been touched off by a nose in consecutive BM66 events at Bathurst and Cootamundra. Already a winner at this circuit in August and Brodie Loy remains aboard. The primary deterrent is carrying 62.0kg (137 lbs) from an outer gate, but the 1100m chute affords a clean run and her canonical 'S' closing kick is formidable on good going.

Closed off strongly when third behind Paparazzo and Abstruse over this trip at Cootamundra last start. Meets Abstruse 4.5kg better at the weights here, carrying just 57.5kg. His sustained swooping 'S' profile is well-suited to Nowra where one-dimensional leaders fold up the final 200m incline.

Designated danger horse. Boasts immense track familiarity (12 starts for 5 placings) and gets the gun economical trip from barrier 2 carrying featherweight 55.0kg. Possesses a sharp closing burst ('C') that peaks when genuine early tempo generates a late meltdown on the uphill stretch.

Enters in winning form after capturing the Bombala Open over 1200m following a courageous BM58 second at Cootamundra. Canonical 'E' front-runner who will press forward from gate 8, but will face hot early pressure from Girls Weekend and faces a testing final 200m uphill at Nowra.

Possesses blistering early gate speed ('E') and draws low to hold the rails. However, she resumes first-up after a five-month spell without an official public barrier trial, and the punishing 405m uphill Nowra home straight historically exposes unconditioned front-runners.

contenders.handicapper_notes: Dominant provincial shipper from the Gerald Ryan and Sterling Alexiou stable. Resumed with an authoritative maiden win at Newcastle over 1250m carrying 57kg, clocking a slick 34.3s final sectional. Ideal low draw in barrier 3, perfectly suited by canonical P stalking style before utilizing the testing 405m Nowra uphill run-in. Top selection.

Warwick Farm visitor trained by Bjorn Baker who arrives race fit and ultra-consistent. Won a maiden nicely over 1300m at Orange two starts ago before sticking on solidly for third in Class 1 grade. Wide draw is minimized by Nowra 1200m chute start, and her stalking P style keeps her right in the finish.

Ciaron Maher-trained 3yo gelding who showed a sharp turn of foot to score first-up at Bathurst over 1100m. Up to Class 1 company now, but possesses significant upside and a lethal canonical S style that will relish launching late down the long 405m Archer Racecourse home stretch.

Local provincial/country runner from the Beer and Carpenter camp. Dominant Moruya maiden winner two back before finishing mid-pack in stronger provincial Class 1 company at Newcastle. First-time blinkers applied today and maps to enjoy a cozy trailing trip from gate 5.

Kerry Parker-trained mare returning from a long spell. Possesses genuine Sydney Metro Saturday and Kembla Grange Benchmark form lines, having competed against much stronger opposition. Faces top weight tax carrying 60.5kg and unproven at 1200m, but raw class makes her the ultimate live threat if forward enough.

David Pfieffer-trained mare first-up following a four-month let-up. Has solid provincial and regional form with a career win and three minors from six starts. Canonical P style puts her in the firing line early, but trials were only fair and may need this outing against sharper race-fit rivals.
